title: [14/10/2025] - Percentage of students giving "very good" rating to resources provided by the college
prompt: The table below shows the percentage of first-year students who gave ‘very good’ rating to the resources provided by their college, for three courses. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The table illustrates the percentage of first-year students who rated various college resources as "very good" for three courses, namely Economics, Law, and Commerce.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, the Commerce course consistently received the highest ratings across all five resource categories. Meanwhile, teaching quality showed the most significant variation among the three courses.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Regarding teaching-related resources, both the Commerce and Economics courses received identical ratings of 95% for teaching quality, significantly higher than Law at 62%, representing a substantial difference of 33 percentage points. For tutor support, Commerce led with 93%, followed closely by Economics at 90%, a mere 3% difference, while Law recorded a notably lower figure of 76%, trailing by 14-17 percentage points. As for pre-course information, Commerce again topped the ratings at 95%, compared to 72% for Law and 59% for Economics, with the latter showing the lowest approval in this category among all three courses.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: Turning to material resources, print resources received an 85% approval rating for the Commerce course, compared to 81% for Economics and 70% for Law, demonstrating a more moderate range of variation between the highest and lowest figures. Finally, other resources showed relatively high satisfaction for both Commerce and Law, at 81% and 80% respectively, differing by just 1 percentage point, whereas only 60% of respondents rated these resources as "very good" for the Economics course, marking it as the least satisfied group in this particular category and creating a 20-21 percentage point gap.
